<action type="say">
Here’s a full draft package for your trip.

--------------------------------
1) Sample schedule (10:00 am – 1:00 pm at the Minneapolis Zoo)
--------------------------------

Adjust times as needed for your actual bus travel.

- 8:45–9:00 am — Departure prep at school
  - Take attendance.
  - Distribute group lists, chaperone assignments, and maps (if you have them).
  - Quick reminder of behavior expectations and what to bring on/off the bus.

- 9:00–9:45 am — Travel to zoo (approximate)
  - On bus: review basic zoo etiquette and any educational focus (ecosystems, conservation, etc.).

- 9:45–10:00 am — Arrival and check-in
  - Buses arrive, students stay seated while teachers check in with zoo staff.
  - Hand out tickets/wristbands if needed.
  - Quick bathroom stop.

- 10:00–10:15 am — Orientation
  - Gather students in a central meeting spot.
  - Brief overview:
    - Schedule (when and where they need to check in).
    - Meeting points and “if you get separated” plan.
    - Any must-see exhibits tied to class content.
  - Confirm group assignments and chaperone responsibilities.

- 10:15–11:15 am — First exploration block (structured focus)
  - Example focus: specific biome(s) or animal groups that align with what you’re teaching.
  - Chaperones lead small groups through a planned route so you hit key exhibits.

- 11:15–11:45 am — Lunch
  - Either:
    - Picnic-style in a designated area, OR
    - Zoo café/indoor eating area if available.
  - Bathroom break at start/end of this block.
  - Quick informal check-in with chaperones on timing/behavior.

- 11:45 am–12:30 pm — Second exploration block (freer choice)
  - Let groups choose a few exhibits of interest within clear boundaries.
  - Optional: simple scavenger hunt or reflection prompts to keep it educational.

- 12:30–12:45 pm — Final meet-up and wrap-up
  - Everyone returns to the designated meeting spot.
  - Attendance.
  - Collect any zoo materials if needed.
  - Short debrief or “one thing you learned/surprised you” share-out.

- 12:45–1:30 pm — Travel back to school
  - On bus: quick written or verbal reflection (e.g., exit ticket questions).

- 1:30 pm onward — Back at school
  - Buffer allows for minor delays while still making “late afternoon” return easily.

--------------------------------
2) Info / permission slip blurb (editable)
--------------------------------

You can paste this into your own document and adjust details like exact times, costs, and your school’s wording.

Title: Minneapolis Zoo Field Trip – 10th–11th Grade

Dear Parents/Guardians,

Our 10th–11th grade students will be taking a field trip to the Minneapolis Zoo to support our learning about [biology/ecology/conservation/insert topic] and to give students a chance to experience real-world examples of the concepts we are studying.

Date: Saturday, December 13, 2025  
Time at Zoo: Approximately 10:00 am – 1:00 pm  
Departure from School: Approximately 9:00 am  
Return to School: Approximately 1:30–2:00 pm  
Location: Minneapolis Zoo, Minneapolis, MN  
Transportation: School bus  
Number of Students: About 60 students (10th–11th grade)  
Chaperones: School staff and approved parent/guardian volunteers

Weather and clothing:
- The forecast currently looks favorable, but this is an outdoor-focused trip.
- Please have your student dress in layers suitable for walking outside and bring:
  - Comfortable walking shoes
  - A light jacket or sweatshirt
  - Sunscreen and a refillable water bottle (optional but recommended)

Meals:
- [Choose one and edit:]
  - Please send a packed lunch that does not require refrigeration or heating.
  - OR Students may bring money to purchase lunch at the zoo (optional; typical meal prices are $____).
- Please ensure any dietary needs are clearly noted below.

Behavior and expectations:
- Students are expected to follow all school behavior guidelines and zoo rules.
- Students must stay with their assigned group and chaperone at all times.
- Use of phones should be appropriate and not disruptive to the group or animals.

Cost:
- The cost for this trip is $____ per student, which covers admission and transportation.
- If the cost presents a hardship, please contact [teacher/office contact] confidentially; we want all students to be able to attend.

Emergency contact:
During the trip, you can reach us at:  
- School contact: [school main phone]  
- Trip lead teacher: [teacher name & mobile number, if appropriate]

Please sign and return the permission form below by: [due date].

I give permission for my student, __________________________, to attend the field trip to the Minneapolis Zoo on Saturday, December 13, 2025, traveling by school bus.

Parent/Guardian name (print): __________________________  
Signature: __________________________   Date: ___________  
Emergency phone number(s): __________________________  
Medical or other important information (allergies, medications, accessibility needs, etc.):  
______________________________________________________  

--------------------------------
3) Planning checklist (concise)
--------------------------------

Logistics & bookings
- [ ] Confirm date and time with the zoo (group reservations, group rates, any required forms).
- [ ] Confirm number of tickets and any chaperone discounts/complimentary tickets.
- [ ] Reserve school buses (specify departure and return times; ensure capacity for 60 students + 6–8 adults).
- [ ] Confirm bus parking and drop-off/pickup procedure with the zoo.
- [ ] Verify any zoo rules for school groups (bag policies, supervision ratios, photography rules, etc.).

Permissions & communication
- [ ] Finalize and distribute permission slip/info letter.
- [ ] Set a permission slip and payment due date.
- [ ] Create a list of students who:
  - [ ] Have turned in permission slips
  - [ ] Have paid/fee waived
  - [ ] Have medical, allergy, or accessibility notes
- [ ] Send reminder emails/messages to families one week and one day before the trip.

Chaperones & supervision
- [ ] Confirm chaperones (6–8 adults total, or as required by your school/zoo ratio).
- [ ] Complete any required volunteer forms/background checks.
- [ ] Assign student groups (ideally 6–10 students per adult, given high schoolers).
- [ ] Share:
  - [ ] Group lists
  - [ ] Schedule
  - [ ] Map of zoo and key meeting points
  - [ ] Behavior expectations and emergency plan with all chaperones.

Student prep
- [ ] Review behavior expectations and group norms in class.
- [ ] Go over:
  - [ ] What to bring/wear (layers, comfortable shoes, water, lunch/money).
  - [ ] What NOT to bring (or rules about valuables).
- [ ] Share educational focus:
  - [ ] Key exhibits to visit
  - [ ] Simple questions/prompts or a short assignment/scavenger hunt.
- [ ] Decide what students will do on the bus (review, reflection, etc.).

Safety & emergency planning
- [ ] Compile a folder/binder with:
  - [ ] Student roster and groups
  - [ ] Emergency contacts
  - [ ] Medical/allergy info and any medications, with instructions
- [ ] Establish:
  - [ ] Primary meeting point inside the zoo
  - [ ] Secondary/emergency meeting point
  - [ ] “If you get separated” instructions for students.
- [ ] Confirm that at least one adult has:
  - [ ] Fully charged phone
  - [ ] First-aid kit
  - [ ] Copies of student medical/emergency info.
- [ ] Check the weather again a day or two before and adjust clothing guidance as needed.

Day-of quick checks
- [ ] Take attendance before leaving school, on arrival, before departure from zoo, and on arrival back at school.
- [ ] Carry contact numbers for:
  - [ ] School office
  - [ ] Bus company
  - [ ] Zoo group coordinator (if applicable).
- [ ] Debrief with students and chaperones afterward (what worked, what to change next time).

If you’d like, I can also help you turn this into:
- A short student-facing expectations handout, or
- A simple scavenger hunt / reflection sheet aligned to your course content.</action>
